abstract: Cellular timing often relies on the accumulation of a regulatory protein to a threshold. For a stable protein produced at a constant rate, the threshold alone sets timing precision: the squared coefficient of variation of the first-passage time is the inverse of the threshold number of molecules. This counting limit appears to be a fundamental constraint. However, production rates vary across the cell cycle. By solving exactly a stochastic model coupling DNA replication and protein accumulation, we show that when a gene replicates at an optimal time, precision exceeds the counting limit.
